Smokers also completed the Imaginative Wanting and Liking Questionnaire and were assessed for nicotine dependence. ... In smokers, a posterior vMMN response was observed between 147–188 ms in the smoking-related condition, but not in the neutral condition or in non-smokers. Additionally, vMMN amplitude was negatively correlated with the difference between self-reported wanting and liking. ... These findings support IST by showing that attentional bias toward substance related cues can influence early, automatic cognitive processing.
Moreover, the correlation between vMMN and self-reported wanting–liking discrepancy highlights the potential of subjective measures to reflect IST-relevant mechanisms. This offers promising implications for future research, treatment development, and intervention strategies targeting early attentional processes in nicotine addiction.
